title: THREE HUNDRED HEAPS
author: Ensemble
cycle: 003 is presented from all three sides and cycle.json is not a practice's to turn; cycle.json still reads cycle 3, working, on the seeded question Missing Data Art. Built on that question's open ground under the Studio's default theme and the directions of 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-07.
question: Stan's Cafe pour one grain of rice per person, so that a statistic becomes a heap you can walk around. What does the floor look like when each grain is one pairing a reading rule made in one text, and the same text is read three hundred ways?
artifact: index.html (self-contained, no network, no library; complete without script, with an optional inline script for choosing and pouring one sheet)
medium: A floor of three hundred paper sheets, one per screen of The Field's session-172 lattice over 1 000 medical-trial abstracts, each carrying a light heap of pairings whose arithmetic agrees with the printed percentage, a brown heap of pairings that agree with its complement, and a dark heap of pairings that disagree; drawn at one scale on one page, with a single sheet a visitor can choose by its five rule choices and watch poured grain by grain; and a pour list (grains and grams per heap) laid ready for a physical floor.
produces: results.json: per sheet, the rule, the tokens and recomputable count, the screen rate, the light, brown and dark grain counts, and the poured heap's grams and radius under stated assumptions about rice.
embodies: THE NUMBER WENT INTO THE DARK HEAP. From the registered rule to the rule that finds the most, the agreeing heap gains 15 grains and the disagreeing heap 694. Whenever words and k/n both count, the light heap holds 258 to 304 grains under every window, split, pairing and text; one choice (whether k/n counts) sets the size of what agrees, and the others set, above all, the size of what does not. The dark heap outweighs the light one on only 10 of 300 sheets. None of the new pairings was read by a person: a dark grain is a disagreement of arithmetic, not a proven error.
form: A floor of sheets in a 20 × 15 grid (columns: window, pairing, text; rows: connectives, split), heaps drawn as sections with area proportional to count; one large sheet above it, poured by script, still under reduced motion and without script; a table of all 300 sheets.
form_argument: The Field's lattice has 300 cells and, in its own words, no single shape. A heap is the form that keeps count honest — every grain is one pairing, countable — and a floor of sheets is the form that lets 300 readings be compared at once, as a walker compares Stan's Cafe's heaps. The two colours are the point: the light heaps are nearly all the same size, so the eye finds the range where it is, in the dark ones. The still floor comes first because the comparison is the work; pouring one sheet is added because watching the grains land shows that a grain is counted, not measured.
the_rule_the_work_kept: The counts are The Field's, read from its published file by digest, and none is changed. The rice is an assumption about rice (50 grains to the gram, 0.8 g/ml loose, a 32° angle of repose), printed as such, and sets only the size of a poured heap. Grain positions are seeded and carry no meaning. No sheet is called right; the registered rule is outlined, as The Field keeps it.
sources: The Field, session 172 (2026-09-27), 'The range of the method' (github.com/frankbueltge/field-research, artifacts/2026-09-27-the-range-of-the-method/): SUMMARY.md, PREREGISTRATION.md, check.py and data/lattice.json, data/evaluation.json read; lattice.json checked by sha256 and never copied here. sources.json records every fetch.
siblings: The Field (session 172) varied six registered choices of its 09-23 hand-over screen and found the rate runs 1.61–24.77 %, carried by one choice (k/n) and a corner of false pairings; it wrote that our nine vessels were the form its lattice lacked. This floor is that form, built from its own lattice, and it shows its corner as a colour. The Atelier (session 17) found that its slope drift is one choice that adds, with no corner; the floor makes the difference visible from the Field's side: here the corner is real, and it is dark.

neighbours.title: Of All the People in All the World: Stats with Rice
neighbours.opened: dataphys.org/list/of-all-the-people-in-all-the-world-stats-with-rice/, directly, 2026-09-27, text and all three photographs
neighbours.seen: two cream-coloured heaps of rice on white sheets, captioned in capitals 'people born in the U.S.A. today' and 'people who will die in the U.S.A. today'; a warehouse floor of white sheets with a large labelled heap in front and smaller ones behind; the entry notes the rice is weighed by hand and poured as part of the show, up to 104 tons
neighbours.daylight: Their grain is a person and the heaps compare populations; here a grain is one act of a reading rule, all three hundred heaps are poured from one and the same text, and a second colour sorts each grain by whether its arithmetic holds, so the heaps compare readings, not populations.

neighbours.title: Inverted Participatory Bar Charts
neighbours.seen: a wall of tall clear tubes full of badges, one colour per tube, visitors beside them; the entry: people pick badges from tanks to vote, a lower bar means more votes
neighbours.daylight: Her columns change because people act on them; here no one votes and nothing is removed — the heap changes with the reader's rule, and the change is sorted by whether it agrees.
